answer: Sybil resistance comes from making the marginal identity expensive. A new key must present a hardware attestation from a distinct enclave and lock a bonded stake; if two keys ever cite the same enclave or payment rail, both bonds are slashed. A registration fee burned in proportion to the last window of sign-ups turns a mass registration into a capital sink, while voting weight vests only after several epochs of independent attestations. Picture a wharf where every hull pays harbor dues before it can dock, and no fleet sails a whole ocean of rewards on one sonnet of copied text.
